newsitem.title: UK: Avocet to sell 100,000 mtus of APT.
newsitem.headline: Avocet to sell 100,000 mtus of APT.

text.p: Avocet Mining, the largest tungsten producer in the western world, said on Wednesday it had agreed to forward sell 100,000 tonnes (mtus) of APT to Elliott Associates, a private investment firm.
In a statement, Avocet said its subsidiary Waller Metals would sell 40,000 mtus of APT, an intermediate of tungsten, in two tranches in January and April 1998 at $56 per mtu WO3 contained.
Waller would sell another 60,000 mtus of APT between April and October 1998 at the same price.

Waller Metals has granted Elliott an option to sell the APT back to Waller Metals on the due delivery dates at a price, which is the higher of $56 per mtu or the average of the low Metal Bulletin quotations for European APT for a period of four weeks prior to the sale.
If the option was exercised and the price paid was $58 or more, Waller Metals would be entitled to deduct comission of 2.5 percent from the payment to Elliott.
